newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to review millennium plans in government.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to review millennium plans in government.

text.p: The opposition Labour party said on Thursday it reserved the right to review plans for a multi-million exhibition to celebrate the Millennium if it wins the forthcoming general election.

Labour's heritage spokesman, Jack Cunningham, said in a letter to the government: "A new Labour government would have the right to review all aspects of the proposals to hold an exhibition at Greenwich to celebrate the Millennium."
The letter was sent to Hayden Phillips, the top civil servant in the Department of National Heritage, the ministry in charge of the project planned in the east of London.
Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine is to meet Labour leader Tony Blair later on Thursday to discuss the plans.
Unless Blair -- tipped by polls to win the election -- agrees to the project, it will be impossible to find the necessary private sector finance for the scheme.
The government wants to make a parliamentary statement agreed with Labour making clear the project will go ahead. But Cunningham said this would have to make clear Labour's views.

Cunningham suggested a clarifying paragraph in the government statement saying Labour was committed in principle to a first-class exhibition but wanted to ensure it is cost effective and properly implemented."
The government said in October the exhibition's centrepiece, a huge dome, was expected to cost 500 million stg. Some 200 million of that is due to come from the National Lottery.
But the rest must be raised from the private sector and costs are thought to have increased since October.
